risks.note: Operations are subject to a long list of sector statutes verified only through management representations in the Secretarial Audit - the Haryana Clinical Establishments Act, Atomic Energy Act and radioactive waste rules, Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, Drugs & Cosmetics Act, NDPS Act, Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, PCPNDT Act, Indian Medical Council and Nursing Council Acts, Food Safety and Legal Metrology laws and the Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act. A lapse in any one can halt a service line or a facility.
risks.risk: Heavy healthcare-specific regulatory and licensing burden

risks.note: Several projects are committed but not yet delivered - the Raipur super-speciality hospital targeted for FY2027, an approximately 650-bed South Delhi facility still only at MoU stage, a new 110-bed Mauritius facility, and roughly 250 additional beds contingent on the Haryana regulatory framework. Delay or cost overrun on any of these defers the capacity and returns underpinning the growth narrative.
risks.risk: Execution risk on a large announced expansion pipeline

risks.note: The Raipur and South Delhi developments are to be funded through a mix of IFC investment proceeds, internal accruals and debt financing, so execution depends on the availability and cost of that debt and on internal cash generation holding up.
risks.risk: Dependence on external funding for growth

risks.note: The ~250-bed addition rests on the Platinum Green Building certification read with a revised regulatory framework introduced by the Government of Haryana; a change in that state framework would directly affect the incremental capacity available at the main location.
risks.risk: Regulatory dependence for bed capacity at the flagship site

risks.note: Growth so far has come from adding towers and beds at one site, which the Company itself frames as building capacity at a single location; that concentrates catchment, referral network and regulatory exposure geographically until Raipur, South Delhi and Mauritius scale.
risks.risk: Concentration in a single flagship location

risks.note: The Board records that the expertise and dedication of the doctors, specialists, surgeons and healthcare professionals associated with the Company remain fundamental to its success - attrition or difficulty in attracting senior clinicians directly affects case mix, complexity and realizations.

The overseas unit at Curepipe, Mauritius is still ramping with utilisation levels only described as improving, and a second Mauritius facility has been announced; overseas ramp-up, market acceptance and jurisdiction-specific compliance are a live watch item.

Risk identification runs through a Board Risk Management Committee and a Risk Management Policy with periodic review and mitigation plans; at the same time the Company is introducing AI-enabled diagnostics and treatment protocols, 5G-enabled ambulances and train/air ambulance services, each of which adds clinical, data and operational risk that the framework must absorb.
risks.risk: Reliance on the enterprise risk framework and technology adoption

sk.overview: The Indian healthcare delivery industry comprises government and private providers offering both in-patient (IPD) and out-patient (OPD) services across primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary care. The market is skewed towards private players due to limited government spending and overburdened state infrastructure, and remains highly fragmented, with large private hospitals accounting for only ~20% of the overall market in fiscal 2025.
